summary: The asset is a quantized subset of Stanford’s 50-dimensional GloVe vectors. The analogy calculation really uses all 50 dimensions and finds queen for king − man + woman. The nearest-word score approximates cosine similarity, and the 3D picture preserves the arrows rather than all distances.

claims.claim: These are named, real 50-dimensional word vectors.
claims.how: Rebuilding the asset from the first 40,000 rows of Stanford’s official GloVe 6B 50D release gives identical bytes. Four original source vectors are also checked directly.

sources.title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation
sources.publisher: Stanford NLP; Pennington, Socher, and Manning
sources.says: The released Wikipedia 2014 and Gigaword 5 corpus contains 6 billion tokens and provides 50-dimensional word vectors. Vector relationships are approximate.

claims.claim: A − B + C is computed over all 50 dimensions.
claims.how: Independent dot-product rankings match queen/throne, rome/milan, large/one, and swimming/diving for four analogies. The input vocabulary has 24,000 entries and the answer search uses 10,000.

claims.claim: Word relationships are approximate rather than universal truths.
claims.how: The retained vocabulary and training corpus determine the answers; queen is the nearest example, not an exact equality or a rule for all words.

simplified: The source is filtered to 24,000 lowercase words and quantized to signed bytes. Answers search only the first 10,000 retained words and exclude the three inputs. The 3D projection rescales axes; it is not a map of every high-dimensional distance.

fixes.what: Normalize each loaded candidate after byte decoding if a future view promises exact cosine ranking.
